ideas.title: Throw a pot, glaze it, open the kiln
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: The strongest pitch here. The glaze isn't painted on: a lubrication solve fills the grooves and breaks off the ridges, and Beer-Lambert depth through that simulated thickness is a material no game engine shows. It also shows off the path tracer, and what the player cuts shows up in the fired jug. The risk is the size of it: a lathe tool, a GPU thin-film solver and a new material in one go. If the first kiln opening doesn't clearly show the player's own lines, it is just a brown jug.

ideas.title: Roast a marshmallow to golden
ideas.critique: A real heat-and-kinetics model of a small, readable skill is a good fit, and the colour creeping round as you turn it is the payoff. But it is a single object with a crust colour, the 'friends rate it' part will probably be scripted, and the film of three marshmallows side by side is a still in all but name.

ideas.title: Dominoes the friends set up all day
ideas.critique: The island already posted a domino chain filmed along its falling front, and this is the same recipe with friends setting them up. Moving it to PrintSim IPC bodies is engine work that viewers can't see. Its real value is as a tipping test for the climbing project, not as a post.

ideas.title: Who stole the pie: follow the footprints
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: A ground that remembers real feet, with a soil response that differs between mud, sand and grass, gives the player something new to read, and a detective goal brings people back. The plainest build is decals stamped at foot contacts with a depth per surface. The 'who stole it' part will be scripted unless the thief really walks there.

ideas.title: Sledging down the snow hill on a tea tray
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
same_form: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: A track that gets faster as it packs is a good loop you play again and again, and racing the friends gives it a goal. But it is the same snow field and the same object sliding downhill as the snowball, which only just missed, so to a viewer it reads as a second snow-slope film.

ideas.title: Push the snowball yourself and build a snowman (snowball project)
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Making the snowball playable is a real step for the project, but building a snowman is the most predictable payoff possible, and the film is again a ball rolling over snow, just with Lumi behind it. Floating or sinking in the sea is a side note, not the new thing.

ideas.title: Giant soap bubbles from a string wand
ideas.nearest: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Thin-film interference read from a simulated draining thickness is exactly what a path tracer can do and a raster can't, and the black spot opening before the pop is a moment people would clip. The minimal-surface pull and the tear-or-close skill give it a goal. It shares its solver with the glaze idea, so whichever is built second will feel less new.

ideas.title: Lumi's feathers are real
ideas.critique: Wet clumping strands and a spin-shake that throws off droplets would give Lumi's body a physical life it has never had, and it counts toward Lumi's own body. There is nothing for the player to do with it, though. If the rods end up as a few drooping cards, all that is left is a mood-driven animation.

ideas.title: Sneak past the owl (owl-ears project)
ideas.critique: This finally gives the owl and the traced hearing a game: different ground means different loudness, which is something to learn and replay. Stealth past a guard that turns its head is a familiar genre, though, and the swoop will be scripted, so the new part is only that the sound is really propagated.

ideas.title: The kites tangle
ideas.critique: Ropes that really collide and wrap, followed by the loss of lift and the spiral, is a new kind of contact for the island, and a small fight in the sky is easy to read. Rod-rod contact under wind load is fragile, though. If the wrap is faked, all that's left is two flying objects falling.
